summary: Commit-window offset produces cohort fracture during gated rollout — tenants routed to degraded fallback
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled gated rollout of rwd-open-13b-v1.2 to NarrativeAI (dedicated pool), a staggered commit-window offset between the control-plane snapshot and the edge prewarm caused a persistent cohort fracture. Several tenant sessions were observed to lose their model pin and be routed to the degraded fallback variant for up to 7 minutes.

Impact:
- ~14% of NarrativeAI's tenant requests in prod-us-west routed to fallback variant (degraded model) for ~4–7 minutes.
- Observed increased token latency and quality regressions for affected sessions.
- Billing spike for customer due to repeated retries and fallback model differential.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted: prod-us-west (dedicated capacity)
- Affected components: orchestrator snapshot commit, edge prewarm, routing-mesh, serving-runtime model bind
- Affected models: rwd-open-13b-v1.2 (primary), rwd-open-7b-v0.9-quant (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (as observed):
1) Schedule gated rollout with commit window at 12:05:00 UTC and staggered edge prewarm completion at 12:06:30 UTC for a subset of edges.
2) Orchestrator commits snapshot epoch N at 12:05:00 but some edge proxies processed shadow prewarm ack at 12:06:30 (offset ~90s).
3) Incoming tenant sessions that established affinity during the 12:05–12:07 window received mixed routing metadata (old epoch route + new prewarm lease).
4) Routing-mesh hit tiebreak path and applied fallback policy, clearing explicit model_pin on session tokens.

Expected behavior:
- Commit and edge prewarm should reconcile within grace window and preserve model_pin for sessions which had an explicit pin request during rollout window.

Actual behavior:
- Model_pin was cleared on a subset of sessions; routing-mesh applied fallback routing rules. Sessions were served by degraded variant until pin reconciliation completed after the background epoch sync.

Logs / evidence:
- Edge proxy logs (edge-az1-12): route_epoch_old=2024-11-08T12:04:59Z, prewarm_ack=2024-11-08T12:06:31Z, pin_probe=missing
- Orchestrator audit: commit(epoch=N) @ 2024-11-08T12:05:00Z; snapshot publish to region us-west @ 12:05:02Z
- Routing-mesh trace id: rm-7a9d34f2 shows tiebreak path -> fallback variant (decision_code=FALLBACK_TIEBREAK)
- Customer telemetry: increased 502 retries and retried request spikes between 12:05–12:12

Workarounds tried so far:
- Support triggered a manual epoch resync on affected edge proxies (partial mitigation) at 12:11, which restored pin affinity for ~60% of affected sessions.
- Suggested customer to defer heavy traffic during the next commit window.

Immediate customer impact and asks:
- Customer wants root cause and assurance this won't recur on future gated rollouts.
- Requesting billing credit assessment for tokens served by fallback during incident window.

Next steps (owner: Diego Ramos):
- Collect full edge logs for all us-west proxies within epoch N to quantify exact affected session count.
- Reproduce in staging by injecting a 60–120s prewarm ack delay and validate routing-mesh tiebreak logic.
- Short-term: tighten commit/prewarm grace window or pause new session acceptance during commit windows (config toggle).
- Medium-term: implement an explicit pin-preservation flag during gated rollout to avoid tiebreak clearance when an explicit pin is present.

Attachments: routing traces, sample edge logs, customer's tokenized request timeline (redacted)

2024-11-08 12:45 - SRE (Diego Ramos): Investigating orchestrator -> edge snapshot propagation. Early hypothesis: snapshot publish acknowledged by control-plane but some edges were still finishing prewarm; routing-mesh tiebreak cleared pin when prewarm lease mismatched epoch. Collecting edge logs now.

2024-11-08 13:12 - Customer (NarrativeAI, CS rep - Maya Liu): We observed degraded responses in user sessions and saw retries. Customer requests timeline + sample request ids attached. Asks for ETA on fix and whether this is rollback-risk for future rollouts.

2024-11-09 09:30 - Orchestrator eng (Priya Singh): Reproduced in staging by delaying prewarm ack by 90s; confirmed routing-mesh falls back when explicit pin_check fails because of epoch mismatch. Patch candidate: ensure pin_probe uses last-known-committed-epoch as tie-break instead of current prewarm lease. Creating PR for review.

2024-11-10 10:05 - Support (Elena Park): PR merged to staging, running SRE validation tests. Coordinating with NarrativeAI for a controlled rerun on their next small rollout window. Billing team looped in for credit evaluation (ticket FIN-1286).
investigation_notes: Edge prewarm ack delay observed only on az1 and az4 (latency due to node drain during maintenance) - correlates with commit window offset.
Routing-mesh decision path uses prewarm_lease timestamp before consulting last_committed_epoch for explicit pins - this ordering caused pin clearance during race.
Quantified affected sessions: preliminary estimate 2,430 requests (14% of customer's traffic in window) across 18 session tokens.
Potential mitigation: treat explicit model_pin header as authoritative during commit windows and defer fallback tiebreak for X seconds.
PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1842 - modifies tie-break ordering and adds integration test for delayed prewarm scenario.
